articles.title: Justin Gaethje’s retirement is closer than you think.
articles.description: Chael Sonnen is in Salt Lake City and has heard enough around the UFC to reconsider something he previously didn't believe: Justin Gaethje may genuinely be considering retirement. Chael explains why Gaethje is in a uniquely clean position to walk away. There is no personal rivalry with Arman Tsarukyan, no announced fight, no obvious No. 1 contender waiting on him and no unfinished business forcing his hand. Unlike other retirement situations where a major matchup was already hanging over the champion, Gaethje could leave without ducking anyone or leaving an obvious fight behind. Chael still wants Gaethje to make whatever decision is right for him. But after previously dismissing the retirement talk, he now believes the possibility that Justin Gaethje has fought for the final time is much more real than most fans realize. articles.title: Why O'Malley vs Talbott Has to Happen Next
articles.description: Peyton Talbot just did something almost nobody does: he beat a 135-pound champion and a 125-pound champion, and now he's calling for Sean O'Malley. Chael breaks down why history says beating a world champion earns you a title shot, why beating two makes it undeniable, and why the bantamweight division's search for new blood makes Talbot the perfect candidate. But there's a catch. Talbot didn't ask for a title shot, he asked for O'Malley. And if Talbot vs O'Malley is a number one contender fight for Talbot, it has to be one for O'Malley too. Chael digs into the matchmaking science nobody talks about, what Henry told him after feeling Talbot's level firsthand, and the uncomfortable question O'Malley is finally asking: what's in it for me? articles.description: Did Chael Sonnen really make $8 million for a fight? Dana White apparently had something to say about that claim. articles.title: How Chael Sonnen got caught using PED's #ufc
articles.description: Even Chael Sonnen—the man known for confidence and relentless trash talk—has experienced genuine fear before a fight. In this clip, Chael recalls walking out to face Brian Stann in Houston, Texas, after Stann had knocked out three opponents. As the curtain opened and his music started, Chael says he froze, thinking, “Please don’t.” He describes the pressure of having to put on his fight-night face and make the walk despite the nerves. The conversation then turns to Chael’s suspension and the evolution of UFC drug testing. He discusses out-of-competition testing, admits he was trying to work around the rules, and explains his perspective on performance-enhancing drugs during a commission hearing. It’s an unusually candid look at the fear, pressure, and mindset behind a major UFC fight—and Chael’s own account of the choices that led to his suspension. Watch as Chael Sonnen reflects on the Brian Stann fight, his walkout nerves, and the drug-testing system. #ChaelSonnen #BrianStann #UFC #MMA #UFCHistory #MMAStories #DrugTesting #PerformanceEnhancingDrugs #FightNight

articles.title: Why One UFC Fight Doesn’t Tell the Whole Story #ufc
articles.description: A fight can last 12 seconds—and that still doesn’t tell you everything about a fighter. Chael Sonnen uses Jorge Masvidal’s famous knockout of Ben Askren to make a bigger point about MMA. Did that one moment prove Masvidal was a better fighter or that he had better skills than Askren? Chael argues that fights can turn on a single moment, and fans shouldn’t let one result create an entire narrative about a fighter. His message to wrestlers is even more direct: don’t abandon what made you successful just because people tell you that you need to become more exciting or completely reinvent yourself. Being well-rounded, entertaining, and marketable can help get you into the Octagon. But once you’re there, Chael says the objective becomes much simpler. You just have to win. #ChaelSonnen #UFC #MMA #JorgeMasvidal #BenAskren #Wrestling #MMAAnalysis #UFCHistory #FightStrategy

articles.title: Why Ilia Topuria Lost to Justin Gaethje #ufc
articles.description: Ilia Topuria had Justin Gaethje hurt—but according to Chael Sonnen, one decision may have changed the entire fight. Chael breaks down Sean O’Malley’s take on the matchup, specifically the moment in the second round when Topuria dropped Gaethje with a body shot. O’Malley believes Ilia could have finished the fight if he had simply walked away instead of following Gaethje to the ground. Chael agrees with the bigger point: Topuria’s year away from competition may have been the difference over 25 minutes. Moving countries, changing gyms, disrupting his training schedule, and returning after a long layoff created a difficult set of circumstances for a fighter trying to maintain championship-level performance. Chael also makes the case for just how decorated Topuria already was—an undefeated UFC champion, former No. 1 pound-for-pound fighter, and two-division champion. He argues that the paperwork surrounding the BMF title may have kept Topuria from adding another championship to his résumé. Was the year-long layoff the real reason Ilia Topuria came up short against Justin Gaethje? #ChaelSonnen #IliaTopuria #JustinGaethje #SeanOMalley #UFC #MMA #BMF #UFCLightweight #MMAAnalysis

articles.title: Daniel Cormier on Alex Pereira NEXT UFC FIGHT announcement: Ulberg, Volkov, Pavlovic, Chimaev?
articles.description: Daniel Cormier IS BACK with a brand new DC Show, this time breaking down UFC superstar Alex Pereira and the potential announcement TODAY of who the heavyweight star will be fighting next. DC believes that his next fight will be at heavyweight, but still feels that Alex would be A PROBLEM at 205 if he was to choose a fight between a top contender or Champion like Carlos Ulberg or Khamzat Chimaev if he chooses to move up a division. DC also speaks on Dana White and the UFC going forward with the Josh Hokit and Ciryl Gane fight, and why he doubles down on that being the fight to make. articles.title: Chael Sonnen was always a heel #ufc
articles.description: Chael Sonnen didn’t become “The Bad Guy” overnight. He says he spent nearly a decade trying to get attention for his fights—and repeatedly got shut down. Looking back at his early UFC years in 2005 and 2006, Chael recalls trying to play the heel while calling out Chuck Liddell and mocking his appearance. In one interview with Sherdog reporter Loretta Hunt, he says she stopped the recording because his persona was so different from what she expected. The interview was never published. And that wasn’t the only time. Chael describes how his college wrestling coach intervened during local newspaper interviews, preventing his provocative comments from reaching print. Without today’s social media platforms, those missed opportunities made it difficult to build a public persona or generate interest in his matches. In this clip, Chael explains the years of frustration behind his fight-promotion style—and how people who didn’t understand his approach kept getting in the way. #ChaelSonnen #UFC #MMA #TheBadGuy #ChuckLiddell #Sherdog #TrashTalk #MMAHistory #UFCStories

articles.title: Dana Got Banned. How Far Does Eddie Go?
articles.description: Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury are finally fighting, fourteen years late, for nothing, and the most interesting man in the whole saga isn't allowed in the building. Eddie Hearn posted the contract verbiage himself: no Zuffa, no TKO, and no Dana White, with Dana named personally so nobody can hide behind an entity. Dana skipped the press conference, reportedly barred by the very contract Hearn put on the internet. Chael watched the presser twice and came away with nothing compelling from either fighter. Turki Alalshikh ran the show with a hot mic the whole time, and Chael still isn't sure who's actually paying for any of it, only that Eddie Hearn never spends his own money. Here's Chael's real take: the fight itself has nothing on it. No belt, no bad blood, both men politely claiming England, fourteen years after anyone asked for it. The only interesting thing about the entire proposition is Hearn versus Dana. And his prediction: this fight scares everybody away. MMA runs 44 weekends a year, and on that night, everyone stays out of the way. articles.description: Josh Hokit doesn’t necessarily need to take Ciryl Gane down to beat him. According to Chael Sonnen, he just needs Gane to believe the takedown is coming. With the November 14 matchup in focus, Chael discusses the different ways Hokit could get the job done, from a knockout to a wrestling-heavy performance. articles.title: Chael Sonnen’s Best Trash Talk Talk (Nogueira Brothers) #ufc
articles.description: Chael Sonnen’s infamous Nogueira brothers joke is one of the most memorable moments in MMA trash-talk history—and it nearly cost him his fighting license. Chael recounts the story of claiming that when the Nogueira brothers first arrived in America, one tried to feed a bus a carrot while the other petted it, believing it was a horse. The absurd insult left the interview host struggling to respond, but the controversy didn’t end with the punchline. Chael says the Nevada executive director at the time threatened to pull his license, arguing that children might look up to him. The twist? Chael insists he used no profanity or threats—just a deliberately outrageous story designed to provoke a reaction. In this clip, Chael explains how the bit was planned, why it was so unusual at the time, and how his approach to trash talk pushed the boundaries of MMA promotion. articles.title: The Dana–Hearn Feud Is Driving Headlines #ufc
articles.description: Is the feud between Dana White and Eddie Hearn becoming a bigger story than Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua? Chael Sonnen breaks down the growing tension between the UFC boss and the boxing promoter, questioning whether their public clash is also generating valuable attention for the heavyweight matchup. He suggests that, whether the conflict is orchestrated or completely genuine, the headlines and interview requests surrounding Dana and Eddie may be drawing more attention than the proposed fight itself. Eddie Hearn has argued that Dana White should have no involvement in the event’s press conferences or promotional activities. Dana, meanwhile, has pushed back, questioning who could stop him from being involved. Chael says he’s reluctant to turn against Hearn, recognizing that promoting the fight is his job. But he also points out that the rivalry between the two promoters is capturing significant attention in North America. Is this a genuine feud, a promotional masterclass, or both? #ChaelSonnen #DanaWhite #EddieHearn #TysonFury #AnthonyJoshua #FuryJoshua #Boxing #UFC #MMA #BoxingNews

articles.title: Justin Gaethje Has a Decision to Make #ufc
articles.description: Arman Tsarukyan has been positioned as the UFC’s leading lightweight contender, and Chael Sonnen says there should be no debate about his place in the title picture. Chael sees that willingness as consistent with the expectations placed on a champion. articles.title: The secret behind Chael Sonnen’s trash talking  #ufc
articles.description: Chael Sonnen didn’t become “The Bad Guy” by accident. He studied what makes a fighter entertaining—and turned it into an art. In this conversation, Chael explains how legendary boxers like Sugar Ray Leonard, Mike Tyson, and Muhammad Ali inspired his understanding of fight promotion. The biggest stars weren’t simply the ones with the best records or the hardest punches. They were the ones who could tell a compelling story and make fans care about what happened next. Chael also breaks down the difference between naturally embracing a heel or face persona and deliberately studying how to build a fight. Drawing on the five W’s—who, what, when, where, and why—he explains why great promotion comes down to great storytelling, not just championships or undefeated records. From professional wrestling’s approach to creating stars to the psychology of fight promotion, this is Chael Sonnen’s philosophy behind the art of the bad guy.
